paras: The police shooting of Smith in San Antonio took place on the morning of January 7, 1882, when Policeman Martinez shot a Black man named Smith in the hip while arresting him as a suspected robber. Smith survived with a flesh wound and was jailed. The case drew a local editorial in the San Antonio Evening Light that criticized arming the police and said Martinez faced a charge of assault with intent to murder.

According to a San Antonio dispatch dated January 7, Smith, who it said had "for some time been engaged in systematical robberies," was caught at daylight that morning by Policeman Martinez. In that account Smith drew a knife, and the policeman shot him in the hip, causing what the dispatch called "Only a flesh wound." Smith was then taken to jail.

Two days after the shooting, the Evening Light wrote that had Martinez killed Smith he would have been guilty of murder, and that "as it is, he will be subject to a charge of assault with intent to murder." No report of a charge, hearing or trial of either Martinez or Smith appears in the coverage.

The same San Antonio telegram ran in the Waco Daily Examiner on January 8 and in the Dallas Weekly Herald and Austin's Weekly Democratic Statesman on January 12, each time among routine local items such as a fatal fall and a large funeral. These printings gave the police version as fact, and the Statesman, which headed the item "Robber Shot," called Smith "The villain" and "The moke," a slur.

The Evening Light, a San Antonio paper, took a different line in an editorial titled "Use of Pistols by the Police." It argued that "a pistol in the hands of a policeman is as dangerous as in the hands of a cow boy," and that an officer may use his weapon only in self-defense, under the same conditions as a private person. The editorial still referred to Smith as "the negro" and "a flying thief," but treated the shooting as a likely crime by the officer rather than a justified act.

The accounts differ on why Martinez fired. The dispatches, which reflect only the police side, said Smith drew a knife after being caught. The Evening Light made no mention of a knife and wrote that Martinez believed his office gave him "a right to shoot down a flying thief," describing a shooting of a fleeing man.

reader.title: Police shooting of Smith in San Antonio
bases: A single city policeman shot Smith while arresting him, with no mob or crowd reported (A1, A2, A3, A4).
A local San Antonio editorial (A2) and the San Antonio dispatches printed in Waco, Dallas and Austin papers (A1, A3, A4) independently agree that Policeman Martinez shot Smith without killing him.

accounts.label: San Antonio dispatch (officer's version)
accounts.gist: Smith, said to be a systematic robber, was caught at daylight by Policeman Martinez, drew a knife, and was shot in the hip, a flesh wound, before being taken to jail.

accounts.label: San Antonio Evening Light editorial
accounts.gist: Martinez believed his office gave him the right to 'shoot down a flying thief'; had Smith died it would have been murder, and Martinez faced a charge of assault with intent to murder.

framing.detail: The Austin Statesman headlined the item 'Robber Shot' and called Smith 'The villain' and 'The moke', reporting the knife as fact.
The Waco Examiner and Dallas Herald printed the same San Antonio telegram without comment among other local items.
The Evening Light's editorial 'Use of Pistols by the Police' said a pistol in a policeman's hands was as dangerous as in a cowboy's and that police may shoot only in self-defense.

versions.value: Smith drew a knife after being caught, and the policeman then shot him
Martinez shot down 'a flying thief', i.e. a fleeing man; no knife mentioned

conflicts.note: The knife version comes from dispatches that give only the police side; the local editorial, written two days later in San Antonio, describes a shooting of a fleeing man and treats it as a likely criminal assault by the officer.

versions.value: 'by forenoon' (possibly an OCR or telegraph variant)

conflicts.note: Both versions place it in the morning.

record_check.record: said to have been engaged in systematic robberies
record_check.dossier: Dispatches state flatly that he 'had for some time been engaged in' systematic robberies; an accusation, not tested in court in the coverage
Drew a knife per the dispatches (police side only); the local editorial describes shooting a fleeing thief instead

record_check.record: ...shot ... while Smith was fleeing... Martinez will face a charge of assault with intent to murder.
record_check.dossier: Fleeing is the editorial's version only, contested by the knife account; the editorial predicted a charge but no report of one being filed was found
